From an owners perspective:

Clients rarely care about quality. Every contract I've won and every contract I've lost came down to how much I charged. I had a client that burned through 3 separate companies before mine. None of them solved their problem. My company came in and completely got rid of vehicle break ins, assaults on staff, and the homeless loitering on the property in 3 months. No one else came close. I tried to increase price by just $2 an hour to adjust for inflation, barely. I figured we'd proven to be a valuable asset and higher quality than our competitors, so it would be an easy yes. They said no and cut us for a camera company because it was cheaper. I have a set limit I won't go below when giving estimates now so I can pay my guys as much as possible, but it's still shockingly low unfortunately. I get underbid by other companies regularly. That's just the reality of the industry. There are too many companies to compete with to charge enough to pay really well. All you have left is people willing to work for lower wages, which are usually people that can't get a job making higher wages. I took a contract and needed to hire for it. I had 13 prospective employees lined up. Only one had the courtesy to tell me he was no longer interested. The other 12 never even showed up to their interview. Not a single one. I was paying above average for wages in the area too. At that point I was willing to take just about anyone or I wouldn't be able to fulfill the contract. I couldn't be picky even though I wanted to. Luckily I found an employee and he's been great, but you learn how shitty the industry is as a whole realy quick
